paragraphs: Choosing initial cluster centers matters for k-means clustering. Both k-means++ and its greedy variant provide starting centers for Lloyd’s algorithm. The greedy version samples several candidates at each step and chooses among them, whereas ordinary k-means++ samples a single candidate. Experiments have repeatedly favored the greedy approach, but existing worst-case theory suggests it can perform worse.

This paper addresses that mismatch by studying a structured class of datasets rather than the most unfavorable possible inputs. Its analysis concerns well-separated clusters whose distributions have exponentially decaying tails, including Gaussian distributions. It also uses a particular candidate count: the number sampled at each step grows proportionally to the logarithm of the number of clusters.

Under those conditions, the authors establish that greedy k-means++ outperforms ordinary k-means++. This gives a theoretical explanation for its practical appeal in the studied setting. The result depends on both the distributional structure and the candidate-count setting; it does not claim that greedy selection wins on every dataset.
neurips-2025-a-beyond-worst-case-analysi.tldr: Greedy k-means++ has a provable advantage on well-separated, exponentially decaying distributions when its candidate count scales logarithmically with the number of clusters.

paragraphs: Groups of language-model agents often depend on a central coordinator to assign work. That arrangement can restrict scaling and adaptation, while making the coordinator a single point of failure. AgentNet proposes a different organization: agents collaborate through a directed network without cycles, coordinating their work without a central orchestrator or predefined workflows.

The framework combines changing network connections with retrieval-based memory. Agents can develop specializations, update their skills through stored knowledge, and adjust whom they connect to as task demands change. Task routing therefore evolves alongside the agents’ capabilities. The design also uses minimal data exchange to support collaboration across organizations while seeking to protect sensitive knowledge.

The reported experiments show improvements over traditional centralized multi-agent systems in efficiency, adaptability, and scalability in dynamic environments. The contribution is a framework in which coordination and specialization can develop together, rather than being fixed in advance. Its privacy-preserving collaboration claim rests on the decentralized design and limited exchange described in the abstract.
neurips-2025-agentnet-decentralized-evol.tldr: AgentNet lets language-model agents specialize, route tasks, and change connections without a central coordinator, improving collaboration in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: AlgoTune asks whether language models can make demanding numerical programs run faster. Instead of evaluating only whether a model reproduces a known solution, it creates an open-ended challenge: write efficient code for problems from computer science, physics, and mathematics. Domain experts contributed the benchmark’s 120 tasks.

The benchmark includes a framework that checks generated solutions and measures their execution time against reference implementations from established open-source packages. The authors also introduce AlgoTuner, a baseline agent evaluated with several frontier language models. This couples code generation with a concrete performance objective, allowing improvements to be assessed against working numerical software rather than judged from the code alone.

AlgoTuner achieves an average speedup of 1.58 times over reference solvers, including implementations from SciPy, scikit-learn, and CVXPY. However, the evaluated models mainly make surface-level optimizations rather than discovering new algorithms. The findings therefore distinguish useful implementation improvements from the deeper algorithmic creativity that the benchmark is intended to encourage.
neurips-2025-algotune-can-language-model.tldr: AlgoTune measures numerical-code optimization, finding that its baseline agent achieves an average 1.58× speedup but mainly through surface-level changes.

paragraphs: Understanding a conversation involves more than recognizing its words. A system may need to identify a speaker’s intention, emotional state, or communicative behavior from multiple kinds of information. MMLA is a benchmark designed to test whether language models and multimodal language models can interpret these higher-level meanings in conversational utterances.

The dataset contains more than 61,000 multimodal utterances from staged and real-world situations. It covers six dimensions: intent, emotion, dialogue act, sentiment, speaking style, and communication behavior. The authors evaluate eight mainstream model branches using zero-shot inference, supervised fine-tuning, and instruction tuning. These settings examine both existing model capabilities and what task-oriented training can add.

Even the fine-tuned models reach only about 60–70% accuracy in the reported experiments. That result indicates substantial remaining difficulty in the tested forms of conversational understanding, rather than establishing a universal ceiling for multimodal models. By releasing the data and code, the authors provide a shared basis for investigating these capabilities more systematically.
neurips-2025-can-large-language-models-h.tldr: MMLA tests six dimensions of conversational meaning across more than 61,000 multimodal utterances, with evaluated fine-tuned models reaching about 60–70% accuracy.

paragraphs: Clinical prediction models increasingly combine several kinds of patient information, but many local sites have only electronic health records and limited training resources. This paper proposes transferring knowledge from a multimodal model trained on a nationwide cohort to smaller local cohorts that have EHR data alone. The transfer crosses both patient populations and available data types.

The framework studies EHR and genetic information as its two modalities. To handle noisy or less useful biological signals, it introduces a mixture-of-aggregations design intended to emphasize informative genetic features. For local adaptation, a lightweight graph-guided fine-tuning method adjusts pretrained representations of EHR-based patient characteristics using limited patient data.

Experiments on real-world clinical data support the effectiveness of the proposed model. The practical significance is that a local site can benefit from knowledge learned with richer data without needing the same modalities locally. The work addresses the adaptation burden directly, combining improved modeling of genetic information at the source with a lighter method for transferring useful representations.
neurips-2025-democratizing-clinical-risk.tldr: The framework transfers knowledge from nationwide EHR-and-genetics models to local EHR-only cohorts through lightweight adaptation.

paragraphs: Resonate-and-Fire neurons use oscillating internal dynamics to extract frequency information and represent it through spikes. These properties make them attractive for long sequences, but their effective memory is limited, and complex temporal tasks expose a trade-off between energy efficiency and training speed. This paper introduces a neuron design inspired by biological dendrites to address those difficulties.

The Dendritic Resonate-and-Fire model separates processing into multiple dendritic branches and a soma, or cell body. Each branch focuses on particular frequency bands, giving the combined neuron a broader frequency representation. The soma also adjusts its firing threshold according to previous spiking activity, aiming to reduce redundant spikes while preserving efficient training.

Experiments show competitive accuracy together with substantially sparse spiking and maintained computational efficiency during training. These findings support the proposed design as a promising approach to efficient long-sequence modeling. The abstract presents edge deployment as a potential application: the reported combination of accuracy, sparse activity, and training efficiency motivates that possibility.
neurips-2025-dendritic-resonate-and-fire.tldr: A multi-branch spiking neuron combines frequency-specific processing with an adaptive firing threshold to model long sequences with sparse activity and competitive accuracy.

paragraphs: Text watermarks modify a language model’s next-token predictions using random side information, such as information derived from earlier tokens. Watermarking becomes particularly difficult when the model strongly favors one next token. In tasks such as coding, this low-entropy setting leaves little flexibility for changing predictions while preserving the quality of the generated text.

The paper develops an optimization framework for deciding how to use that random information effectively. Its objective balances making the watermark detectable against distorting the generated output. The resulting designs, HeavyWater and SimplexWater, expose a tunable trade-off between detection accuracy and text distortion. They can be applied to any language model and do not require a particular method of generating side information.

Across the reported benchmarks, both methods can achieve high detection accuracy with little loss of generation quality, especially in low-entropy settings. The theoretical analysis also identifies connections to coding theory. The contribution combines a principled design framework with watermark mechanisms that accommodate different priorities for detection and output quality.
neurips-2025-heavywater-and-simplexwater.tldr: HeavyWater and SimplexWater use an optimization-based design to balance watermark detection and text distortion, especially when next-token predictions are nearly deterministic.

paragraphs: Recent efficient sequence models improve their recurrent memory through the Delta learning rule. In models such as Gated DeltaNet, TTT, and RWKV-7, interactions between the memory state and a key vector create a bilinear recurrence. This paper organizes those models under the concept of Bilinear RNNs and analyzes their strengths and limitations.

The authors then introduce Comba, a variant informed by closed-loop control theory. It uses a state transition made from a scalar component plus a low-rank component, together with corrections based on both state feedback and output feedback. The central idea is to use feedback explicitly in the recurrent update, making memory management part of the model’s control structure.

To make the design computationally practical, the authors implement a chunk-wise parallel kernel in Triton and train models with 340 million and 1.3 billion parameters. Reported language-modeling and vision results show superior performance and computational efficiency. The contribution therefore combines an analysis of recurrent architectures, a feedback-based model design, and an implementation suited to efficient computation.
neurips-2025-improving-bilinear-rnn-with.tldr: Comba applies state and output feedback to a bilinear recurrent architecture, reporting improved performance and computational efficiency on language and vision tasks.

paragraphs: Quantized language models store weights at low precision, but fine-tuning often adds higher-precision adaptation weights. This mismatch can reduce inference efficiency and introduce approximation error when the adaptations are merged back into the quantized model. LoTA-QAF addresses the mismatch by designing adaptation weights specifically for the quantized representation.

Its adaptation uses ternary weights aligned with the quantization grid, allowing the updates to merge without additional loss from approximation or truncation. The method can adjust all quantized weights and uses ternary signed gradient descent to update the adaptations. Here, lossless merging describes preservation of the adaptation during merging; it does not assert that quantization itself has no effect on model accuracy.

Experiments cover the Llama-3.1/3.3 and Qwen-2.5 families. On MMLU, LoTA-QAF recovers quantized-model performance and exceeds 16-bit LoRA by up to 5.14%. The comparison changes for task-specific fine-tuning: 16-bit LoRA performs better, although LoTA-QAF still surpasses the other methods tested. Its appeal therefore combines exact merging with competitive, task-dependent results.
neurips-2025-lota-qaf-lossless-ternary-a.tldr: LoTA-QAF aligns ternary adaptations with quantized weights for lossless merging, improving MMLU recovery while trailing 16-bit LoRA in task-specific fine-tuning.

paragraphs: Biomedical assistants may need to understand images, answer questions, and produce reports containing both images and text. Existing training datasets offer limited scale, task coverage, or source diversity. MedMax addresses this training-data problem with a mixed-modal instruction dataset containing 1.47 million instances across multiple biomedical domains.

The dataset includes tasks involving alternating images and text, biomedical image captioning and generation, visual conversation, and report understanding. Its coverage includes radiology and histopathology, with material grounded in medical papers and YouTube videos. By bringing these tasks into one dataset, the authors support training a single foundation model for several forms of biomedical interaction.

After fine-tuning a mixed-modal foundation model, the authors report a 26% gain over Chameleon and an 18.3% improvement over GPT-4o across 12 downstream biomedical visual question-answering tasks. These comparisons establish gains on the stated evaluation tasks. The work also introduces a unified biomedical evaluation suite and releases the dataset, model, and code to support further development.
neurips-2025-medmax-mixed-modal-instruct.tldr: MedMax supplies 1.47 million mixed-modal biomedical training instances and yields reported gains across 12 biomedical visual question-answering tasks.

paragraphs: Answering questions about a table can require several linked operations, such as extracting entries, comparing values, and calculating a result. These steps become harder when the table is an image rather than structured text. Turbo tackles this visual reasoning problem by using clean structured table data during training, while requiring only the table image at test time.

The structured data acts as privileged information: it helps teach the model how visual evidence connects to logical steps. A reasoning-trace generator based on DeepSeek-R1 uses table structure to produce explanations that bridge the visual and structured representations. Turbo repeatedly generates and selects useful traces to strengthen the multimodal model’s reasoning.

Using 9,000 training examples, Turbo reports state-of-the-art results across multiple datasets, with a stated 7.2% improvement over the previous best. The approach matters because it transfers support available during training into a model that must later reason from images alone. Its central contribution is linking table appearance to reasoning steps through structured supervision.
neurips-2025-multimodal-tabular-reasonin.tldr: Turbo uses structured tables during training to teach image-based table reasoning, reporting a 7.2% improvement over prior state-of-the-art results with 9,000 examples.

paragraphs: Natural Gradient Variational Inference approximates posterior distributions by optimizing a simpler distribution. Although widely used, its convergence theory is less developed for non-conjugate models, where the objective can be non-convex. This paper studies that setting under a mean-field parameterization, which structures the approximate distribution into separate components.

The authors first derive sufficient conditions for relative smoothness: a way to control how the objective changes using geometry defined by a suitable mirror map. They then modify the algorithm with non-Euclidean projections. Using this structure, they prove a finite-iteration convergence guarantee toward a stationary point. Such a point need not be a global optimum in a non-convex problem.

A stronger result requires additional structural assumptions on the likelihood. Under those assumptions, the authors identify hidden convexity and establish fast global convergence to a global optimum. The paper therefore separates two levels of guarantee, showing how the available mathematical structure determines whether convergence reaches stationarity or the best possible objective value.
neurips-2025-natural-gradient-vi-guarant.tldr: The paper gives conditional convergence guarantees for non-conjugate natural-gradient variational inference, with global optimality requiring additional likelihood structure.

paragraphs: Recent sensory experience can bias current perception in opposite directions. Repulsion moves perception away from an earlier stimulus, while attraction pulls it toward that stimulus. This paper develops a two-layer continuous attractor neural network to explain how both effects could arise from short-term changes in synaptic behavior at different processing stages.

The lower layer represents sensory processing and is dominated by synaptic depression. Sustained depletion of neurotransmitter produces repulsion in the model. The higher layer represents processing after perception and is dominated by synaptic facilitation, where an elevated probability of neurotransmitter release produces attraction. The time constants of these mechanisms determine how long each bias persists.

The model explains serial-dependence patterns observed in visual orientation judgments and provides a neural basis for a Bayesian interpretation of those patterns. Its contribution is a mechanistic account linking two opposing perceptual effects to different forms of short-term synaptic plasticity. Within this account, sensory sensitivity and later cognitive stability emerge from distinct but coordinated processing layers.
neurips-2025-neural-correlates-of-serial.tldr: A two-layer neural model explains perceptual repulsion and attraction through synaptic depression and facilitation operating at different processing stages.

paragraphs: An image may need several watermarks for different purposes, such as ownership information and content provenance. Those marks must remain detectable and decodable when embedded together. This paper studies whether deep image-watermarking methods can coexist, examining a situation in which separate watermark systems share the same media.

The authors find that various open-source watermarks can coexist with only small effects on image quality and decoding robustness. This empirical result suggests that combining watermark systems need not cause severe interference in the tested settings. It also motivates treating multiple watermarking methods as an ensemble, using their combined behavior to provide capabilities beyond a single method.

The paper shows that ensembling can increase total message capacity and offer new trade-offs among capacity, accuracy, robustness, and image quality. These combinations do not require retraining the underlying watermark models. The contribution is therefore both an investigation of compatibility and a way to reuse existing methods when an application needs a different balance of watermarking properties.
neurips-2025-on-the-coexistence-and-ense.tldr: Several tested image watermarks coexist with minor interference, enabling ensembles that increase message capacity and offer new trade-offs without retraining.

paragraphs: Historical control data could make an A/B test more informative, but the historical and experimental populations may differ. Combining them therefore requires deciding how much to trust each source. This paper studies that decision through an estimator that combines two causal-effect estimates constructed using experimental and historical datasets.

The central move is to treat the combination’s weighting function as a policy. That reformulation makes existing pessimistic policy-learning algorithms available for choosing the weights. The goal is to minimize the combined estimator’s mean squared error, so the integration decision is tied directly to the accuracy of the resulting effect estimate rather than to a fixed mixing rule.

The authors compare their method with baseline estimators through theoretical and empirical analyses spanning five scenarios. Both forms of analysis find near-optimal performance across those scenarios. The result supports learning how to combine the sources while accounting for their distributional differences. The near-optimality claim applies to the scenarios analyzed, preserving the importance of the setting in which historical information is reused.
neurips-2025-pessimistic-data-integratio.tldr: The method learns how to weight historical and experimental causal estimates using pessimistic policy learning, achieving near-optimal performance in five analyzed scenarios.

paragraphs: Some modern 3D reconstruction models predict pointmaps directly from image pairs without requiring known camera parameters or scene geometry. Their performance nevertheless depends on the amount and variety of training data. Puzzles addresses this data constraint by generating posed video-depth training examples from a single image or video clip.

The augmentation applies targeted image transformations to simulate varied camera trajectories and realistic scene geometry. This creates an unbounded supply of synthetic variants from limited source material, expanding the training variety available to existing reconstruction pipelines. Because Puzzles changes the training data, it can be incorporated without altering the underlying network architecture.

The reported experiments find consistent improvements when Puzzles is added to video-based 3D reconstruction pipelines. Notably, training with only 10% of the original data plus the augmentation achieves accuracy comparable to training on the full dataset. This demonstrates substantial data efficiency in the evaluated settings and highlights synthetic variation as a practical way to strengthen reconstruction training.
neurips-2025-puzzles-unbounded-video-dep.tldr: Puzzles synthesizes varied video-depth training data, allowing evaluated 3D reconstruction models to match full-data accuracy using 10% of the original data.

paragraphs: Compiler optimization can make neural-model serving faster, but the search space is enormous and its decisions are interdependent. A transformation that helps in one program state may interact differently with later choices. Reasoning Compiler investigates whether an existing language model can use this context to guide optimization more efficiently without retraining.

The framework treats compilation as a sequence of decisions and combines language-model proposals with Monte Carlo tree search. The language model suggests hardware-informed transformations using the current program state and accumulated performance feedback. Tree search then balances investigating new possibilities with pursuing promising choices, organizing the search around the proposals rather than exploring transformations without that guidance.

The authors report substantial speedups with markedly fewer evaluated samples than leading neural compilers. The finding supports the usefulness of language-model reasoning as a proposal mechanism within a structured search procedure. Its contribution is the combination: contextual suggestions guide the choices, while tree search manages how those choices are explored over multiple optimization steps.
neurips-2025-reasoning-compiler-llm-guid.tldr: Reasoning Compiler combines an unretrained language model with tree search to find faster neural-program compilations using substantially fewer search samples.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning with rewards only for correct answers depends on a model having some initial chance of solving a problem. This paper shifts the training objective toward teaching. Its Reinforcement-Learned Teachers receive both the question and its solution, then learn to produce explanations that help a student understand how the solution follows.

Rewards come from giving each explanation to the student and testing the student’s understanding of the solution. This provides dense feedback about teaching effectiveness while avoiding the need for the teacher to discover the answer through exploration. The resulting model is optimized for downstream distillation, making explanation quality depend on its usefulness to the learner.

The raw outputs of a seven-billion-parameter teacher yield higher final performance on competition and graduate-level tasks than existing pipelines using processed traces from much larger models. The teachers also remain effective for larger students and zero-shot transfer to out-of-distribution tasks. These findings support training specifically for teaching as an efficient and reusable component of reasoning-model development.
neurips-2025-reinforcement-learning-teac.tldr: Reinforcement-Learned Teachers use known solutions and student feedback to learn explanations that improve distillation, with strong results from a seven-billion-parameter teacher.

paragraphs: Data points from different sources may have different probabilities of being corrupted. This paper studies robust estimation when those probabilities are known, differ across samples, and govern independent corruption events. That setting captures a form of uneven reliability that methods based on a single corruption rate or a worst-case rate can overlook.

The authors establish tight minimax rates for estimating means of multivariate bounded distributions and one-dimensional Gaussian distributions across all heterogeneous corruption patterns. Minimax rates describe the best achievable worst-case estimation error in the specified setting. For multivariate Gaussian mean estimation and linear regression, the squared-error characterization is accurate up to a factor equal to the square root of the dimension.

The results also suggest that optimal estimators may discard samples whose corruption probabilities exceed a threshold. That threshold depends on the empirical distribution of the supplied corruption rates, rather than being a universal cutoff. The work shows how knowing the pattern of reliability can change both achievable accuracy and which observations are worth using.
neurips-2025-robust-estimation-under-het.tldr: The paper characterizes robust estimation with known, unequal corruption probabilities and shows why sufficiently unreliable samples may be discarded.

paragraphs: Gradual domain adaptation moves a model from a source distribution toward a different target distribution through intermediate domains. Existing methods often use self-training, but knowledge transfer can be inefficient or intermediate data incomplete. Self-Training with Dynamic Weighting addresses the transition by changing how strongly source and target objectives influence training.

The method generates pseudo-labels from the model’s own predictions and uses them for iterative updates. A time-varying parameter progresses from zero to one, controlling the balance of domain-specific loss contributions. This scheduled weighting is intended to make the movement toward the target domain stable while maintaining robustness across the intermediate domains.

Experiments on rotated MNIST, color-shifted MNIST, portraits, and Cover Type show improvements over existing baselines. Ablation studies support the importance of the dynamic schedule in reducing domain bias and improving generalization. The contribution is a training framework that manages the strength of adaptation over time, with theoretical insights and empirical evidence supporting its use for gradual distribution changes.
neurips-2025-self-training-with-dynamic-.tldr: STDW progressively reweights source and target training losses during self-training, improving gradual domain adaptation on the reported datasets.

paragraphs: Matching motion sequences with text is difficult when one sequence contains several coupled actions or movement concepts. Aligning only the overall motion with its description can leave the correspondence between individual concepts ambiguous. SGAR addresses this problem by decomposing human movement into finer semantic units associated with body parts.

The framework uses the prior knowledge of existing language models to support that structural decomposition. It then applies part-mixture learning to separate local motion concepts and improve alignment at the body-part level. A directional relation alignment strategy also connects full-body and part-motion representations, encouraging the learned representation space to remain consistent across those scales.

Experiments across three benchmarks show superior performance and promising transfer to recognition and generation applications alongside motion-text retrieval. The significance is that the framework organizes alignment around explicit motion structure instead of relying only on whole-sequence concepts. Its reported transferability suggests that learning these finer correspondences can support several motion-understanding tasks in the evaluated settings.
neurips-2025-sgar-structural-generative-.tldr: SGAR decomposes motion into body-part concepts to improve motion-text alignment, with reported gains in retrieval and transfer to recognition and generation.

paragraphs: Linear dynamical systems describe sequences through an evolving internal state. This paper studies symmetric systems and presents an identification method whose accuracy guarantees do not depend on the system’s state dimension or effective memory. The approach builds on a representation in which these systems behave as convolutions learnable through fixed spectral transformations.

SpectraLDS supplies the reverse step: recovering a dynamical-system model from that spectral representation. This inversion yields an end-to-end convex optimization procedure. The resulting distillation preserves predictive accuracy while producing a model that can process each token using constant time and space with respect to sequence length.

That efficiency statement concerns how inference scales as a sequence grows; the separate accuracy guarantee concerns state dimension and effective memory. The authors evaluate SpectraLDS inside sequence-prediction architectures, including language-modeling tasks, and find preserved accuracy with improved inference efficiency. The contribution links a tractable learning representation to an efficient recurrent form, supported by both theoretical guarantees for symmetric systems and empirical sequence-prediction results.
neurips-2025-spectralds-provable-distill.tldr: SpectraLDS recovers symmetric linear dynamical systems from spectral representations, preserving predictive accuracy while enabling inference costs per token independent of sequence length.

paragraphs: Entropy minimization makes a model place more probability on outputs it already favors. This paper finds that this simple objective can improve reasoning on difficult mathematics, physics, and coding tasks without labeled data. It investigates whether stronger concentration of existing predictions can bring out capabilities already present in pretrained models.

The authors test three mechanisms. EM-FT reduces token-level entropy while fine-tuning on unlabeled outputs sampled from the model. EM-RL uses negative entropy as its only reinforcement-learning reward. EM-INF adjusts prediction logits during inference, requiring neither training data nor parameter changes. These approaches apply the same broad objective at different stages of model use.

On Qwen-7B, EM-RL matches or exceeds strong RL baselines trained on 60,000 labeled examples. On SciCode, EM-INF lets Qwen-32B match or exceed the named proprietary models while being three times more efficient than self-consistency and sequential refinement. These empirical results support entropy reduction as a way to elicit reasoning capabilities in the tested models and tasks.
neurips-2025-the-unreasonable-effectiven.tldr: Reducing output entropy improves reasoning in the reported evaluations without labeled data, including an inference-only method that requires no parameter updates.

paragraphs: Tasks such as tracking and robotic manipulation require visual representations that capture how a scene changes over time. Token Bottleneck, or ToBo, learns such representations through a self-supervised prediction task. It compresses a reference scene into a single token, then uses that token to help predict a subsequent scene.

Training has two stages: squeezing the reference scene into the compact representation and expanding it to predict the target scene. During expansion, the model receives only a few patches from the target as hints. The design encourages the visual backbone to encode temporal dependencies, since the compressed reference information must help account for the transition to the later scene.

Experiments show improvements over baselines on sequential tasks including video label propagation and simulated robot manipulation. Physical-robot deployment also supports the pretrained model’s robustness and effectiveness in real environments, and evaluations cover different model scales. The contribution is a simple training constraint that encourages compact visual representations to retain information useful for understanding dynamics.
neurips-2025-token-bottleneck-one-token-.tldr: ToBo learns temporal visual representations by compressing a scene into one token and predicting a later scene with only a few visual hints.

paragraphs: Diffusion models can learn features useful for recognition even though they are designed to generate data. A recurring observation is that feature quality peaks at an intermediate noise level, producing a curve with a single peak. This paper investigates why that pattern appears and what it reveals about the model’s learned distribution.

The theoretical analysis uses the low-dimensional structure underlying image data. It shows that the single-peaked behavior emerges when the diffusion model successfully captures the underlying distribution. The explanation involves the interaction between denoising strength and confidence about class identity across noise levels, connecting representation quality to the model’s behavior along the denoising process.

In classification experiments, the authors find that this curve also reflects generalization. The single peak appears when models generate novel images, while the curve gradually becomes monotonically decreasing as models begin memorizing training examples. The findings connect a feature-quality measurement to generative behavior, providing an empirically supported indication of generalization in the studied setting.
neurips-2025-understanding-representatio.tldr: The paper explains why diffusion features can peak at intermediate noise and finds that this pattern tracks generalization versus memorization in classification experiments.
